s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic inflammatory condition of the nails and mucosa with possible autoimmune or infectious etiology
salient_findings: Painful swelling of the proximal nail folds
Dripping of blood from fingernails and toenails
Lichenoid plaques and erosions on the oral mucosa
Violaceous discoloration and longitudinal ridging of the nails
Raised liver enzyme levels and positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status
key_facts: Male patient in his 60s
Symptoms present for the last year
No history of preceding trauma or drug intake
Proximal nail folds are swollen and show violaceous discoloration
Nails show longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation
Partial to complete loss of nail plate with oozing of blood and hemorrhagic crusting
Oral mucosa shows lichenoid plaques and erosions
Raised liver enzyme levels
Positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status
Histopathology shows hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, and basal cell degeneration
Dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of lichenoid plaques on oral mucosa, violaceous discoloration of proximal nail folds, and histopathology showing hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, and basal cell degeneration

shortlist.label: Hepatitis C-associated lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and clinical presentation consistent with lichen planus

shortlist.label: Necrolytic acral erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Raised liver enzyme levels and violaceous discoloration of proximal nail folds, which are characteristic of this condition

shortlist.label: Psoriatic nail dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Nail changes such as longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation, which are consistent with psoriatic nail dystrophy

shortlist.label: Chronic hepatitis C infection
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and raised liver enzyme levels, which suggest a chronic hepatitis C infection

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including painful swelling of the proximal nail folds, lichenoid plaques on the oral mucosa, and histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, and basal cell degeneration, are consistent with lichen planus. Additionally, the patient's positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and raised liver enzyme levels suggest a link between the patient's lichen planus and hepatitis C infection.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms are consistent with lichen planus, the presence of hepatitis C infection suggests a more specific diagnosis of hepatitis C-associated lichen planus.

rejected.label: Necrolytic acral erythema
rejected.why: This condition is also associated with hepatitis C infection, but the patient's symptoms and histopathological findings are more consistent with lichen planus.

rejected.label: Psoriatic nail dystrophy
rejected.why: The patient's nail findings, such as longitudinal ridging and thinning, are not typical of psoriatic nail dystrophy, and the presence of lichenoid plaques on the oral mucosa is not consistent with psoriasis.

rejected.label: Chronic hepatitis C infection
rejected.why: While the patient has chronic hepatitis C infection, this diagnosis does not explain the patient's dermatological symptoms, which are better accounted for by hepatitis C-associated lichen planus.

gold: Bullous lichen planus of the nails
